translate_en|mods/TrueSleepEverywhere/42: Disabled: the game sleeps the way it always did, standing up.
Lie down on beds and couches
Sleeping on a bed, a couch, a bench or a booth lays the survivor on it: head on the pillow for a bed, body along the seat for a couch. Chairs, armchairs and stools keep the game's sitting pose.
Sleeping on the ground (or on a sleeping bag, hay...) sits the survivor down and really puts them to sleep, instead of leaving them standing.

Sitting on a chair, an armchair or a couch with a firearm in hand, you can aim and shoot without getting up (poses built from the game's own sitting and aiming animations). You stay put while the gun is up.
Sleeping on a chair, an armchair, a stool or a toilet: the survivor sits down, the head droops, and they fall asleep sitting. The bathtub is one of the game's (bad) beds: normal sleep, standing.
Sleep or rest against a wall

Right-click a square next to a wall, a window or a fence: "Sleep against the wall" and "Rest against the wall". The survivor sits down with their back to the wall; asleep, the head drops. Resting is the same pose without sleeping (endurance comes back as when sitting on the ground). Doors do not count.
